<cite ref="Bava Batra 21b:7">B. Bath. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>קא פַסְקַת וכ׳</he> thou cuttest off (interferest with), v. <cite ref="H00691"><he>חַיּוּתָא</he></cite>.

Lev. R. s. 32, end פסקת חייוי דהאי גברא thou cuttest off (shortenest) this man’s (my) life (by divulging my spurious descent); a. fr.—פסיק רישיה ולא ימות ‘let his head be cut off, but let him not die’, a dialectic term for an unavoidable result of an act.

<cite ref="Shabbat 75a:6">Sabb. 75ᵃ</cite> <he>מודה ר״ש בפ׳ ר׳ וכ׳</he> R. S. (who ordinarily permits, on the Sabbath, an act which may have as a result a violation of the Sabbath law, if the latter is not intended) admits that such an act is forbidden, if the result is inevitable.
Targ. Hos. II, 8 (ed. Lag. Af.).—
<cite ref="Pesachim 111a:4">Pes. 111ᵃ</cite> <he>פַּסְקִינְהוּ רשות הרבים</he> (Rashb. <he>פְּסַקְתִּינְהוּ</he>) the public road divides them (the two palms); a. e.—
Meg. 2ᵇ; B. Kam. 65ᵇ, v. infra Af.

<cite ref="Moed Katan 4a:15">M. Kat. 4ᵃ</cite> <he>מיא דלא פּסְקֵי</he> water which never fails.
<cite ref="Moed Katan 4a:19">Ib.</cite> <he>עבידא דפַסְקָא</he> it often fails.

<cite ref="Moed Katan 18b:20">Ib. 18ᵇ</cite> <he>קלא דלא פָסֵיק</he> a continuous rumor; <he>וכמה קלא דלא פ׳</he> how long must a rumor last to be called a continuous rumor? <cite ref="Moed Katan 18b:20">Ib.</cite> <he>דלא פ׳ ביני ביני</he> if it has not ceased at intervals.
<cite ref="Gittin 69a:7">Gitt. 69ᵃ</cite> <he>כי היכי דפסקי … לִיפְסוֹק וכ׳</he> as this water ceases to run, so may the blood of—stop flowing.

<cite ref="Ketubot 65a:9">Keth. 65ᵃ</cite> <he>פְּסוֹק לי מזוני</he> give me an order for my food; <he>פ׳ לה</he> he did so. Ib. 63ᵃ <he>פסקו ליה וכ׳</he> they made arrangements for him for six years (to remain at college).

Meg. 2ᵇ אתא את ואַפְסְקיה וכ׳ Ms. M. (ed. ופסק, ופסיק) the eth (וְאֵת, Esth. IX, 21) comes to divide the sentence (giving it the meaning) that some celebrate the fourteenth and others the fifteenth of Adar.

B. Kam. 65ᵇ את פַּסְקֵיה קרא with eth (ואת, Lev. V, 25) the text separates the clause from the preceding, opp. ערביה combines it; Yalk. Lev. 479 את אַפְסְקֵיה eth separates it; ib. לאַפְסוּקֵי בין ממון וכ׳ (not לאפסוקיה) to draw the line between sacred property and &c.

<cite ref="Sotah 38b:20">Sot. 38ᵇ</cite> <he>אריכי … לא מַפְסְקֵי</he> tall persons in front of short ones do not form a partition (to intercept the priestly benediction pronounced upon the congregation); <he>תיבה לא מַפְסְקָא</he> nor does the Tebah (v. <cite ref="V00035"><he>תֵּבָה</he></cite>) between the priests and the people form a partition.
<cite ref="Pesachim 111a:6">Pes. 111ᵃ</cite> <he>אַפְסְקִינְהוּ בעפרא</he> he dammed it (the waste water poured out in the street) with dust (spread dust over it); a. fr.—
